comment: Failures of core's page test project (scripts/ci/page-tests.mjs) that are accepted, each with the reason. `where` covers any test that throws in that function of a bundled file; `suite` with `test` covers one test; `suite` alone covers a whole suite. `kind` is `not-reached` (the page bundles the function and never calls it: `why` says how that is known), `no-environment` (the test sets an environment variable, and the page has none, so the function answers as if it were unset) or `bug` (the page does reach it; not fixed yet).

entries.why: Uses os.homedir, path and fs to read git config, after returning early when the call has no `cwd`. The page never passes one: gui/src/redux/thunks/evaluateToolPolicies.ts (callContextFor) adds `cwd` only when `process` exists, and headsUp.ts and startToolTimers.ts pass `parsedArgs` alone. Those are the only callers of levelOfCall in gui/src.

Reads process.platform. The one caller in gui/src, callContextFor in redux/thunks/evaluateToolPolicies.ts, calls it only after `typeof process !== "undefined"`. The other bundled importers of shell.ts (candidates.ts, readOnlyCommand.ts, shellScan.ts) take isPosixShell only.
Uses Buffer. Bundled through shell.ts and containerArgs.ts, where it builds the arguments of a shell that resolveShell returns, and the page does not call resolveShell (see that entry).
Sets CONTINUE_TERMINAL_ENV. In the page `process.env` is `{}`, so the setting from config.yaml stands, which is what the settings page should show.

entries.why: Uses createHash from node:crypto. Its only caller is core/tools/permissions/auto/handler.ts, which runs in core when the page sends tools/autoReview; the page imports handler.ts for a type only, and from state.ts only stableStringify (gui/src/redux/slices/blockedCallsSlice.ts). The planMode suite reaches it by calling the handler directly.
